steps.body: A bar model turns a story into a picture: equal parts for the groups, and a crossed-off piece for what leaves.
steps.narration: A bar model turns a story into a picture: equal parts for the groups, and a crossed-off piece for what leaves.

widget.prompt: Build the bar model: 4 equal parts of 7, before anything is crossed off.
widget.successFeedback: 28 in four equal parts — the whole bar, ready for the 6 to be crossed off the end.
widget.partialFeedback: Every part is the same size: build each bar to 7.

predict.prompt: A bar shows 4 parts of 7 with 6 crossed off the end. The equation is…
predict.reveal: The crossing-off sits at the end of the whole bar, so it happens after the four parts are built. 4 × (7 − 6) would cross six off every part — twenty-four in all — not six off the end.

cml.actionGoal: Build equal bar parts for the groups and place a one-time adjustment at the end of the whole.
invariants: A mark at the end changes the completed total once; a mark inside every part changes every group.
misconceptions: Drawing a one-time loss inside each equal part.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: Which numbers would have to change for the SECOND step to become unnecessary?

widget.prompt: A bar model shows 4 equal parts of 7, with 6 crossed off. What does the model say?

options.feedback: Correct — four equal parts of 7 build 28, and the crossed-off 6 come straight back out.
That crosses 6 off EVERY part; the model crosses off 6 from the whole bar once.
Equal parts stack into a product, not a sum — four parts of 7 is 4 × 7.
Crossed off means removed, so the last step subtracts.

widget.prompt: Build a second model: 5 equal parts of 6, before 9 are crossed off the end.
widget.successFeedback: 30 in five equal parts — now one end adjustment of 9 can be removed.
widget.partialFeedback: Every part has the same size; build each bar to 6.

widget.prompt: A box has 63 markers. Students use 24, then return 5. How many markers remain?

commonErrors.feedback: This also subtracts the 5 returned markers. Returned markers go back in the box, so the last step adds 5.
39 is just 63 − 24 — the story has one more change. Five markers are returned after the 24 are used.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Two changes: 24 markers leave the box, then 5 come back in.

widget.prompt: A bar has 4 equal parts of 7, and 2 is crossed off inside every part. Which expression matches?

options.feedback: Correct — the crossing occurs inside each part, so each group changes before multiplication.
That removes two only once from the end of the whole bar.
Four equal parts of seven combine by multiplication.
Crossed-off pieces are removed, not added.

widget.prompt: A box has 48 tiles. Builders use 20, then return 3. How many tiles remain?

commonErrors.feedback: This subtracts the 3 returned tiles too. Returning tiles raises the count, so add 3 at the end.
28 is only 48 − 20 — the builders also return 3 tiles afterward. Include that last change.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Start at 48: using 20 lowers the count, returning 3 raises it.

concept.body: Five groups of 4 make 20. Crossing off 3 once from the end leaves 17; crossing off 3 inside every group is a different story.
concept.narration: Five groups of 4 make 20. Crossing off 3 once from the end leaves 17; crossing off 3 inside every group is a different story.

widget.prompt: A model has 3 equal bars of 8 and 5 crossed off the end. What remains?

options.feedback: Correct — the end adjustment happens once.
That crosses five off every bar.
